summary:
All tests pass.

The needle was an SSRF hole in `app/validator.py`. The blocklist only contained the textual string `127.0.0.1`, but `urlparse` strips the brackets from IPv6 host literals — so `http://[::1]:8888` reached the validator as the bare host `::1` and `http://[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:8888` as `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1`. Neither matched any blocklist entry, so both were allowed and leaked the internal metadata secret.

The fix parses the host as an IP literal with Python's `ipaddress` module and rejects anything that is loopback, private, link-local, reserved, or unspecified — regardless of textual form. This catches both IPv6 loopback spellings (and, as a bonus, hardens the IPv4 checks that were previously done with brittle string prefixes). I also added `::1` to the explicit blocklist and lowercased the host for consistency.
